selection_process.description: The strict goal is the highest-quality publicly available learning resources per topic. Initial selection preceded scoring; the matrix now preserves all original candidates and adds omitted teaching-oriented alternatives. Each criterion has evidence, pedagogy and definition references have distinct roles, licensing is separate, and source-selection-review.md records internal decisions and unresolved gaps. No independent expert review has occurred or is required as a prerequisite.

criteria.check: The source teaches the exact concept the Study Day requires; relevance is justified in selection_rationale with the specific section or timestamp used.
Required prior knowledge is stated so the source can be placed on the correct Study Day without hidden gaps.
Preference for sources with practice material, worked examples, or runnable code the learner can verify locally.

Author is identifiable and accountable (official documentation, university course, named author with revision history); claims in the excerpted portion can be checked against a second source or by executing code.
Author, original_url, and source_type are recorded; derived or excerpted content keeps a link back to the original.
version_or_verification_date records which edition was reviewed and when; fast-moving tools are re-verified before statements about flags or versions are repeated in content.

license and permission_basis are recorded per source. reuse_category stays at 'linking' unless the license explicitly permits excerpting; video subtitles and transcripts are never imported or redistributed without explicit rights.

process: 1. Enumerate candidates for the Study Day concept, including at least one alternative recorded in compared_candidates.

2. Compare candidates against the seven criteria above using only verifiable facts; block-level 1-5 scores are recorded in curriculum/sources/comparison-matrix.json (license text, dated documentation, executable examples).
3. Select primary sources and record a bounded selection_rationale stating what the source contributes, not why it is superior in general.
4. Record known_availability_limitations and a safe_fallback so a removed or paywalled source does not break the Study Day.
5. On re-verification, update version_or_verification_date; if the source changed materially, re-run the rubric before keeping it.
